title: Evidence Model
abstract: The document specifies how CHOIR represents an evidence item, how evidence items are typed by pramāṇa , and how they are aggregated in support of a claim §2, §3, §4 . Its central commitment is that evidence items are not independent, and that treating them as if they were is "the dominant source of overconfidence in rule-based systems" §1 — so aggregation runs over an independence partition rather than over an item list §4.4 , with defeasible structure settled before any grading is applied §5.1 . The source carries its own status line, Draft for review ; this publication is drafted but not accepted as specification, and per MANIFESTO.md every research document is a hypothesis.

sections.heading: Abstract
sections.html: The document specifies how CHOIR represents an evidence item, how evidence items are typed by pramāṇa, and how they are aggregated in support of a claim (§2, §3, §4). Its central commitment is that evidence items are not independent, and that treating them as if they were is "the dominant source of overconfidence in rule-based systems" (§1) — so aggregation runs over an independence partition rather than over an item list (§4.4), with defeasible structure settled before any grading is applied (§5.1). The source carries its own status line, Draft for review; this publication is drafted but not accepted as specification, and per MANIFESTO.md every research document is a hypothesis.

sections.heading: Research Question
sections.html:
The source states the problem directly in §1: institutional reasoning accumulates, and "the model must say how that accumulation works." A conclusion is "rarely licensed by one rule; it is supported by several, opposed by others, qualified by exceptions, and weighted by the authority of its sources" (§1). The question is therefore how to accumulate evidence for a claim without the naive method — count supporting items, count contradicting items, subtract — which the source says fails on a specific and pervasive problem, stated in §1 as a displayed claim:

Evidence items are not independent, and treating them as if they were is the dominant source of overconfidence in rule-based systems.

The source names its own centre of gravity: "§4 is the core of this document, and correlation handling is the reason it is long" (§1).

sections.heading: Finding
sections.html:
Evidence is data plus a bearing relation

Per computational_primitives.md §3.11, cited in §2, evidence is not data: "Data is raw; evidence is data plus a bearing relation to a specific claim." The record carries id, claim, polarity, weight, pramāṇa, derivation, independence, source, context, valid_time, defeated_by, and status (§2). Two properties of the schema are asserted in the surrounding prose: weight is "derived, never authored", and defeated_by entries are "marked, never deleted". The claim field is mandatory "because the same observation is evidence for one proposition and irrelevant to another. Storing evidence without its claim produces a pool of facts that cannot be aggregated" (§2). The independence field is labelled in the schema itself as "the critical field".

The typology follows pramāṇa, because acquisition determines defeat

§3 adopts the pramāṇa framework of vedic_reasoning_methodology.md §2, on the stated ground that it "turns out to be a better fit than the usual source-type taxonomies because it classifies by how the knowledge was acquired, which is what determines its defeat conditions."

TypePramāṇaAcquisitionDefeated by
directpratyakṣaObservation / measurement / chart inputInstrument error; misreading
derivedanumānaRule applicationDefeat of the rule or its inputs
analogicalupamānaStructural correspondence to a precedentDisanalogy in a relevant respect
attestedśabdaStatement in an authoritative sourceSource authority challenge; misreading
abductivearthāpattiBest available explanationA better explanation
absenceanupalabdhiNon-observation where observation was expectedFailure of the observability condition

Three consequences are drawn. attested is first-class (§3.1): "In every domain CHOIR targets, textual authority is a primary means of knowledge, not a fallback. A statute is the evidence. A śāstric verse is the evidence." This is why source-authority ranking (conflict_resolution.md §5.3) is "central machinery rather than a tiebreaker" (§3.1). analogical evidence must record the mapped correspondences and the relations not mapped, because "an analogy without stated limits cannot be defeated by disanalogy, and an undefeatable defeasible inference is a contradiction in terms" (§3.2).

absence carries the observability condition

§3.3 restores a restriction on anupalabdhi that the source says "modern closed-world reasoning routinely drops":

Non-apprehension licenses denial only where apprehension would have occurred had the thing been present.

Formally, absence-evidence is admissible only where the context declares the relevant domain complete: Absence(P) is admissible in context C iff C.completeness_declaration covers domain(P). Without the declaration, "'not observed' means unknown, not false" (§3.3).

DomainWhere the declaration is safeWhere it is not
JyotiṣaPlanetary positions — the chart is complete by constructionYogas: the corpus is not exhaustively extracted
LawAn exhaustive statutory listCase law — always potentially incomplete
MedicineA completed test panelUndocumented history

The Jyotiṣa row is called instructive (§3.3): "Jupiter is not in a kendra" is sound absence-reasoning because the chart fixes all positions; "No cancelling yoga is present" is not sound unless the cancellation corpus is complete — which, per rule_extraction_framework.md §2.1, it typically is not. The source notes that this is "exactly the gap canonical_shloka_analysis.md §9.2 reports as incomplete_defeater_analysis rather than concealing." It also records a limit on its own machinery: who declares completeness is unresolved (vedic_reasoning_methodology.md §8.4), and "the declaration is itself an authority claim and should carry provenance" (§3.3).

Independence is computed, not estimated

§4.1 distinguishes three derivation classes: direct (independent unless the instrument is shared), derived (shares the ancestry of its inputs), and inherited (fully dependent on the parent). Inherited evidence is called "the most dangerous, because it multiplies effortlessly": if a property inherits down a class hierarchy, "every subclass instance appears to contribute fresh support for a claim about the parent — a straightforward double count" (§4.1).

Every item therefore carries an IndependenceKey identifying "what it ultimately rests on" — root_sources, root_rules, kernel_versions (§4.2). "Two evidence items are independent iff their keys are disjoint. They are correlated to the degree their keys overlap." The source argues this is computable rather than estimated, because the derives_from closure is already maintained for the traceability invariant (computational_primitives.md §3.16), and "the independence key is the same closure, projected onto roots." It draws the design conclusion explicitly: "Correlation detection comes free from a mechanism the system needs anyway — which is a strong argument for the reification-heavy storage design in knowledge_graph_spec.md" (§4.2).

§4.3 adds that content addressing (reasoning_ontology.md §7.2) unifies two textual statements of the same rule into one rule with two provenance records, which is "a genuine independence signal: two texts, two transmission lines, one rule" — as against two rules derived from the same verse, which are "same root source, fully correlated, no additional support." The system distinguishes these "without a heuristic, because the identity scheme already does."

The source records a hard case it cannot solve. §4.3: textual dependence — text B copies text A — yields two provenance records that are not independent transmissions. "Detecting this requires philological stemma information — which text descends from which — and that is domain-expert input, not computation. The model provides the field (source.stemma_parent) and cannot populate it automatically."

Aggregation runs over clusters, and is deliberately conservative

§4.4 specifies aggregation over the independence partition, not the item list:

1. Partition evidence for a claim into correlation clusters
   (items sharing root sources / rules)
2. Reduce each cluster to a single effective item
   — weight = strongest in cluster, NOT the sum
3. Aggregate across clusters using a saturating operator

Step 2 is described as "deliberately conservative": five restatements of one rule contribute what the strongest single statement contributes. They may raise interpretive confidence — "the tradition evidently agreed" — but do not multiply inferential support, and the two axes stay separate (confidence_framework.md §3).

Operators assessed, and two rejected outright

§5 assesses candidate aggregation operators and records negative verdicts:

ApproachFitVerdict
BayesianRequires priors and a likelihood model. Neither is available for a normative corpus — there is no base rate for "a statute means X"✗ Not as the primary operator
Dempster–ShaferRepresents ignorance explicitly (a genuine advantage), but Dempster's rule behaves pathologically under high conflict, producing counterintuitive results precisely where conflict matters most✗ Rejected on that failure
Subjective logicOpinion triples ⟨belief, disbelief, uncertainty⟩; handles ignorance without the conflict pathology; supports source discounting✅ Good fit for the graded layer
Argumentation (Dung / ASPIC+)Determines which arguments survive attack. Exactly right for defeasible structure; but binary — no gradation✅ Good fit for the structural layer
Weighted votingSimple, explainable; ignores structure and correlation entirely✗ Too naive alone

The decision in §5.1 is two layers, in a fixed order:

Structure first, then gradation. Never both in one number.

Layer 1 is structural (argumentation): which arguments survive defeat, output a set of surviving arguments, binary and explainable. Only survivors proceed to Layer 2, which is graded, correlation-aware and saturating: how strongly the survivors support the claim, output a graded opinion with an uncertainty component (§5.1).

The stated reason for the ordering is that "defeat is not a matter of degree. An undercut inference is withdrawn, not weakened (canonical_shloka_analysis.md §9.2). Folding defeat into a weight makes a defeated inference contribute a small positive amount, which is both wrong and unexplainable — the system would be saying 'this rule was cancelled, so it counts slightly.'" Layer 1 also produces the material the explanation needs — what attacked what, and what survived (explainability_framework.md §5).

§5.2 imposes a saturation requirement: aggregate(e₁ … eₙ) < ceiling(strongest_evidence_class). "A conclusion supported only by weak indications is capped below one supported by a primary attested rule, regardless of count. Without this, the system can be talked into certainty by volume — the characteristic failure of additive scoring schemes."

Polarity separates "counterbalanced" from "irrelevant"

§6 keeps supporting, contradicting and balanced all stored against the claim and all informative, while irrelevant items are not stored at all. Collapsing these into one "neutral" value "conflates 'we looked and it cuts both ways' with 'this has nothing to do with the claim.' The first is a finding; the second is noise." balanced is identified as the evidential counterpart of satpratipakṣa (vedic_reasoning_methodology.md §2.2) — "the tradition's name for a genuinely counterbalanced reason" — and it feeds the vikalpa outcome in conflict_resolution.md §7.

Strength is derived from structure

§7 holds that evidence weight is derived from structural properties, never authored (computational_primitives.md §3.14): evidence type sets a type-specific ceiling; source authority scales weight via a domain-supplied ranking (L2, per reasoning_ontology.md §2.1); rule specificity raises weight when a rule fires, so lex specialis acts "as a weight, not only as precedence"; derivation depth attenuates, because "each defeasible step compounds uncertainty"; extraction confidence caps the weight, because one "cannot rely more on a rule than on the reading of it"; and attestation independence raises interpretive weight only, not inferential weight (§4.3). The source underlines the depth rule: "a conclusion four defeasible inferences deep is weaker than one directly supported, even if every step looked strong. Long chains are where rule systems quietly become fiction" (§7).

Nothing is deleted

§8 gives the lifecycle — proposed → admitted → active, branching to defeated (marked, retained), superseded (new version) or withdrawn (source retracted), with rejected recorded with a reason. Defeated evidence is never deleted (knowledge_graph_spec.md I5), for three stated reasons: the explanation must say what was considered and rejected, since "a conclusion reached after weighing contrary evidence differs from one reached in ignorance of it, even when the conclusion is identical"; defeat is context-relative, so evidence defeated in one context may be live in another; and defeaters can themselves be defeated (nīca-bhaṅga), "which restores the original — and restoration is impossible if the evidence was removed." Withdrawal is distinguished from defeat: withdrawn evidence is also retained, but conclusions depending on it "are flagged for re-derivation rather than merely re-weighted" (§8).

Worked example: the correlation discount, quantified once

§9 works the evidence supporting forms(Gajakesari) in Chart A, taken from canonical_shloka_analysis.md §9.1:

#EvidenceTypePolarityIndependence root
e1Rule gajakesari_formation firedderivedsupporting{source: TBD-verse, rule: gajakesari_formation}
e2position(Guru) = Karkadirectsupporting{chart_input}
e3position(Candra) = Meṣadirectsupporting{chart_input}
e4debilitation defeater not firedabsencesupporting{ontology:debilitation_table}
e5combustion defeater not firedabsencesupporting{kernel:combustion, chart_input}
e6exalted(Guru, Karka)attestedmodulating{ontology:exaltation_table}

The correlation analysis (§9): e2 and e3 share chart_input and form one cluster, because "two positions from one chart are not two independent observations of the yoga's formation"; e1 derives from e2 and e3 and joins the same cluster, since "e1 is not additional support, it is the conclusion of that cluster"; e4 and e5 rest on different roots and are independent of each other, but admissible only under the observability condition of §3.3 — the chart is complete for positions, so both are sound, while "no other cancelling condition exists" would not be sound and "is correctly not claimed"; and e6 is an influence, not support for formation (computational_primitives.md §3.7), which "modulates the strength of the indication and must not enter the support tally."

The result is one effective supporting cluster, two independent absence confirmations, and one positive modulation. "Naive counting would have reported five supporting items, and would have overstated the warrant roughly fivefold" (§9). The source states this factor for this one worked chart; it does not report a measured error rate over a corpus.

Status of this document

The source is marked "Draft for review" and is a Phase 3 (Institutional Reasoning) research document. It is drafted but not accepted as specification, and per MANIFESTO.md every research document is a hypothesis. Several of its central mechanisms are stated as designs rather than as implemented and measured behaviour: the Layer 2 fusion operator is not fixed (§10.6), the cluster reduction policy is chosen on conservative grounds rather than on evidence (§10.1), and the stemma field cannot be populated automatically (§4.3).

sections.heading: Architectural Implications
sections.html:
The source reserves the DAALE boundary daale/ontology/evidence.py for this model, and records that it fills choir/research/R003_Evidence_Representation.md, which is currently empty (header).

For storage: the independence key is the derives_from closure projected onto roots (§4.2), so correlation detection requires no separate mechanism, and the source treats this as "a strong argument for the reification-heavy storage design in knowledge_graph_spec.md" (§4.2). Content addressing (reasoning_ontology.md §7.2) must remain the identity scheme, since it is what distinguishes genuine independent attestation from restatement without a heuristic (§4.3).

For execution: aggregation cannot be a single scoring pass. §5.1 requires an argumentation layer that settles defeat first and a graded layer that runs only over survivors, and forbids combining them into one number. The graded operator must be saturating (§5.2) and must operate on clusters rather than items (§4.4). Layer 1's attack/survival record is the material that explainability_framework.md §5 consumes.

For the ontology: weight must be derived, never authored (§7, per computational_primitives.md §3.14); claim must be mandatory on every evidence item (§2); evidence must never be deleted, only marked (§8, per knowledge_graph_spec.md I5), because nīca-bhaṅga restoration depends on retention; and balanced must be a distinct stored polarity, since it feeds the vikalpa outcome in conflict_resolution.md §7 (§6). Interpretive and inferential confidence must stay on separate axes (§4.4, per confidence_framework.md §3).

For domain configuration: source-authority ranking is domain-supplied (L2, per reasoning_ontology.md §2.1) and is central machinery, not a tiebreaker (§3.1, §7). Contexts must be able to carry a completeness_declaration, since an entire evidence type — absence — is gated on it (§3.3), and that declaration should carry provenance because it is itself an authority claim.

sections.heading: Open Questions
sections.html:
The source records six open questions in §10, and further unresolved points in the body.

  1. Cluster reduction policy (§10.1). §4.4 takes the strongest item in a cluster; an alternative is a within-cluster diminishing sum. "The conservative choice is taken because overconfidence is the failure mode being guarded against, but it may under-credit genuine partial independence."
  2. Textual stemma (§10.2). §4.3 cannot detect copying between texts without philological input. "How much of the corpus this affects is unknown and could be substantial."
  3. Completeness declarations (§10.3). "Who may declare a domain complete for absence-reasoning, and with what authority? Unresolved, and it gates a whole evidence type." §3.3 records the same gap, referring to vedic_reasoning_methodology.md §8.4.
  4. Is balanced stable under re-evaluation? (§10.4). Evidence balanced at one point may become unbalanced when more is extracted; whether balance should be recomputed or recorded as of a decision time "interacts with the tri-temporal model."
  5. Cross-context aggregation (§10.5). Whether evidence from a more general context contributes to a specific-context claim (lattice-upward closure) "is the same open question as knowledge_graph_spec.md §8.2, and it has a large effect on evidence volume."
  6. Subjective-logic parameterisation (§10.6). §5 selects the family; "the specific fusion operator (cumulative, averaging, weighted) is not fixed, and the choice matters for how independent sources combine."

Additionally, the source notes that the cancellation corpus for Jyotiṣa is typically not complete (§3.3, per rule_extraction_framework.md §2.1), which is the gap canonical_shloka_analysis.md §9.2 reports as incomplete_defeater_analysis; and that the worked example's independence root for e1 carries a placeholder source, TBD-verse (§9).
